# AGENTS.md

## Project

GridPlayer is a cross-platform PyQt5 desktop app for playing multiple videos side-by-side, backed by VLC. Python 3.10+, using `uv` and `just`.

## Hard boundaries

* **Do not create commits or push changes unless explicitly requested by the user.**
* **Compiled resources are generated.** `gridplayer/resources/` is generated by `just generate-resources` from the raw sources in `resources/`. Do not hand-edit it; regenerate after changing raw resources.
* **Translations are managed externally.** Do not modify `.ts`/`.qm` files, `scripts/translations/*`, or run any `just translations-*` recipe.
* **Vendored VLC code:** `gridplayer/vlc_player/vlc.py` is vendored. Do not modify it.

## Setup & common commands

```bash
uv sync
uv run gridplayer
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
```

## UI files

Files matching `*_ui.py` are generated from Qt Designer `.ui` sources. Never edit them directly. Edit the `.ui` source in `resources/ui` instead, then run:

```bash
just generate-ui
```

## Test harnesses driving the real app

Closing the player asks "do you want to save?" by default, and a harness has
nobody to answer it, so it hangs forever after the main window closes. Set the
playlist to discard before building the player:

```python
from gridplayer.params.static import UnsavedChangesMode
from gridplayer.settings import Settings

Settings().set("playlist/unsaved_changes", UnsavedChangesMode.DISCARD)
```

## Video block parts

`VideoBlock` (`gridplayer/widgets/video_block.py`) keeps the core: loading,
playback, seeking, rate and its Qt events. Everything else lives in a part, a
`VideoBlockPart` subclass in its own `video_block_<part>.py`, kept on the
block as an attribute: `status`, `bookmarker`, `view`, `chapters`,
`sponsorblock`, `subtitles`, `audio`, `loop`, `screenshot`, `recovery`,
`stream` and `navigation`.

* A part reaches its block through `self._block`. When moving a method into
  a part, every `self.x` that is the block's must become `self._block.x`. A
  bare `self` passed on (to a dialog, a signal, `ctx.commands`) has to become
  `self._block` too; a test with a `Mock` block will not notice.
* The `only_initialized` / `only_seekable` / ... guards in
  `video_block_guards.py` work on part methods as well; they ask the block.
* Commands name part methods with a dot: `("active", "navigation.next")`,
  `LOADING_COMMANDS` entries, `manual_seek("bookmarker.seek", i)`. An
  `("all", "x")` command emits `VideoBlocksManager.all_x`, which
  `VideoBlocksManager` connects to `vb.<part>.<method>` for each new block.
  `tests/test_dotted_commands.py` checks that every named command resolves.
* Parts are made in `VideoBlock.__init__` before `init_url_resolver()`,
  which connects to them. A new part goes there too, and into
  `_block_parts()` in `tests/conftest.py`.
* In tests, `mock_block_parts(block)` gives a `Mock(spec=VideoBlock)` its
  parts, and `is_block_command("part.method")` checks a command name. A part
  that makes a `QTimer(block)` cannot take a `Mock` as its parent: patch
  `gridplayer.widgets.video_block_<part>.QTimer`, or use a `QObject`
  stand-in.
* An exception raised inside a Qt slot aborts the whole test run ("Fatal
  Python error: Aborted"), not just the test.

## Translatable strings

`pylupdate5` only extracts a string when it sees a literal context and a
literal text in the call itself. Anything else still translates at runtime if
the entry happens to exist, but never reaches translators.

* Always write `translate("Context", "Text")` (or `self.tr("Text")`) with
  string literals at the call site.
* Do not add wrapper helpers such as `_t(text)` / `_tr(text)`, and do not pass
  the context through a constant or variable.
* Do not put `tr()` / `translate()` inside f-strings; translate first, then
  format or concatenate.
* Do not call `translate()` at import time in modules loaded before
  `init_translator()` (see `tests/test_translation_timing.py`).
* A choice or toggle shown both in the menu (`params/actions.py`,
  `player/managers/active_block.py`) and in the settings form
  (`params/defaults_fields.py`) uses one context named after the setting
  (e.g. `Transform`, `When Finished`, `Playlist Settings`). Other menu strings
  use `Actions`; other settings form strings use `SettingsDialog`.

## Code style

* Follow the Ruff configuration in `pyproject.toml`.
* Tests live in `tests/`.
